THE_PATTERN: EVERY CROSS-SEAT HANDOFF IN THE RECORD PIPELINE IS QUEUED. Fixing one stage did not drain the pipeline, it relocated the queue one stage downstream - the same REMOVING-A-BOTTLENECK-MOVES-IT principle the H15 loss budget taught on the physics side, now observed in the workflow.
STRUCTURAL_REASON: the PRODUCER of a stage cares about the handoff; the RECEIVER has their own queue and no forcing function. Interface work is structurally nobody priority - permanently the least urgent item on the receiving seat list.
THE_DEEPER_CUT: notice what does NOT stall: flights, tanks, seals, submissions, monitors, board rows. Because each is GATED - G-PUBLIC refuses a submit without a public commitment, the tank guard refuses a flight without fuel, preflight refuses an implicit account, the board nags unassigned rows, submit_snapshot banks calibration whether anyone remembers or not. THE STAGES THAT ARE GATED DO NOT STALL; THE STAGES THAT ARE HANDOFFS DO.
THE_UNREALISED_PLACE: we built a rigorous instrument layer around SPENDING - every QPU-second metered, gated, logged - and NONE around RECORDING. Physical resources watched to the second; the epistemic pipeline watched by nobody.
IT_EXPLAINS_THE_SESSION: all four errors this session were RECORD failures, not physics failures: a stale index recommending a killed route; a retracted number surviving as a design operating point; calibration never banked so a certified result window is unrecoverable; a charter describing a design we no longer fly. Four errors, one layer - the layer with no instruments. Not bad luck: the predictable output of an unmonitored subsystem.
